case_name: Federation of Directly Appointed Officers of Indian Railway and Others v Union of India and Others
petitioner: Federation of Directly Appointed Officers of Indian Railway and Others
holding: The distinction between the two services was well marked in Katyani Dayal's case 1980 Indlaw SC 319 (supra) and the important question of equality was once for all settled. To find fault with it, at this juncture again on the touch-stone of equality dimension would be to unsettle a settled position.
The rule of weightage also appears to us to be reasonable and this is a pattern which has been noticed and approved in many a Service.

A dispute now sought to be raised under Article 32 of the Constitution between the Officers in a representative capacity and Engineers across also in a representative capacity must be held to be barred by principles of res judicata as also in the rule of constructive res judicata.
We thus leave the matter as it is.
No compelling reasons to deviate from the principles enunciated in the judgment.
